tasks.title: gridui-debt Dialog font-derived min-width needs Style min_width
tasks.description:
**Rescued from the old root `HANDOFF.md` §3c (deleted 2026-07-13); do not lose this.**

A short confirm dialog ("Delete Pane?") renders **cramped** — the panel hugs its content, so a two-word title + two buttons produces a tiny box, and dialogs of different content have visibly different widths with no shared baseline.

## The gap
`Style` (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs`) has **no `min_width`** — only `width`/`height` (`Length::{Auto, Px}`). So `Dialog` cannot express "hug the content, but never below a sensible floor".

## Work
1. Add `min_width: Length` (and probably `min_height` for symmetry — decide) to `Style`, defaulting to `Length::Auto`, and wire it into `Style::to_taffy()` (taffy has `min_size`). Add the builder to `LayoutExt`.
2. Give `Dialog`'s panel a **font-derived** minimum — the note said **~22em** (i.e. `22 × base font`), so it scales with the theme font instead of being a magic pixel count. Verify against the real dialogs (delete-pane confirm, the rename form).
3. Tests: a `min_width` smaller than the content is a no-op; larger than the content floors the box; it scales with the base font.
4. `docs/widgets.md`: the `Style`/`LayoutExt` tables + the `Dialog` entry.

## Why it's here
`gridui-07` (crate-review debt) is the right home: it is a missing primitive in the layout style, not a feature.

## Gates
clippy 0; `cargo test -p heca-grid-ui -p heca`; showcase green; no `cargo fmt`.

tasks.title: A proportional share must not be written as a fixed measure
tasks.description:
# The problem

To make two containers take half a region each, `with_share` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs`) writes:

```rust
layout.flex_grow = grow;
layout.height = heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0);      // ← a FIXED measure
layout.min_height = Some(heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0));
layout.flex_shrink = Some(1.0);
```

**A proportional share is being expressed by writing a fixed number**, which is what the user does not
want anyone doing (2026-07-28: *"I don't want other developers to write fixed measure"*). Worse, it is
three coupled fields whose combination is folklore: get one wrong and the split silently reverts to
content-sizing, which is exactly the bug it was written to fix.

# Why it is there

`flex_grow` distributes only **positive free space**. Container content is routinely taller than a
sidebar, so there is no positive free space to distribute — measured 2026-07-28: two containers took
**1214px each inside a 600px body** and divided nothing. In CSS the answer is `flex: 1 1 0`; the base
size of 0 is what makes the whole region free space. With it: **296px each**, measured.

**`Layout` has no `flex_basis`** (confirmed — `grep flex_basis heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs` is empty),
so `height = Px(0)` is standing in for it. taffy *does* have `flex_basis` in its `Style`, so the
concept is available one layer down and simply was never surfaced.

# What to build

1. **Add `flex_basis: Option<Length>` to `Layout`** and map it in `to_taffy`
   (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs`). That is the missing word in the vocabulary; everything below already
   understands it.
2. **Give the library one way to say "take a share"** so no caller assembles the trio by hand — a
   builder on `LayoutExt` (`heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs`), e.g. `share(n)`, meaning *n shares of the
   parent's main axis*, setting grow + basis 0 + min 0 + shrink internally. Then:
   - `with_share` becomes one call and stops naming a measure;
   - the SDK's `Style` trait (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) exposes the same thing, so a **described** tree
     can say it too — today it can only set `flex_grow`, which has the same trap;
   - `grow()` stays as the raw flex knob for callers who genuinely want content-based basis.
   Decide whether `grow()` should be *renamed* or documented as the low-level one, so the obvious name
   is the one that behaves as expected.
3. **Main-axis, not height.** `flex_basis` is main-axis relative like `flex_grow`, so one setter covers
   a column and a row (the same reason `ContainerContribution::grow` is not called `height_grow`). Do
   not add a per-axis variant.
4. **Sweep for the same folklore elsewhere.** `ScrollRegion::new()` already sets `min_height: 0` and
   `flex_shrink: 1` by hand with a long comment explaining why (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/scroll_region.rs:274`).
   Check whether that is the same idea written a second way, and whether it should go through the new
   setter.
5. **Tests must measure, not inspect flags.** A test asserting `flex_grow == 1.0` passed while the
   layout was visibly broken (2026-07-28) — the measured-height test is what caught it. Assert
   pixels: two shares of a 600px region are ~296 each, with content far taller than either.

# Acceptance

- No caller writes a fixed measure to express a proportion — not in `heca`, not in the SDK, not in a
  described tree.
- One setter, documented, with the trio behind it.
- `docs/widgets.md` says how to take a share, next to R8 (the stretch contract) in
  `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` — the two rules are read together.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

tasks.title: Collapsing an ItemGroup piles its rows on top of each other above the group
tasks.description:
**Reported by Antonio, driving the showcase, 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10, with screenshots.** Collapsing EXPLORER or SOURCE CONTROL in the showcase's sidebar leaves the group's row text drawn **overlapping itself**, stacked above the collapsed group — several file names rendered on top of one another at the top-left of the frame ("chrome_region.rs" over "showcase.rs" over "old_sidebar.rs"), while the group header itself draws correctly.

**This predates the 2026-08 event-model work** (F004/P084/T394/T395/T400) — it survived a full revert of T400's decision 2 unchanged, so do not look for it there.

# Where to look

`ItemGroup` (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/item_group.rs`) collapses by setting `style.layout.hidden` on the rows (taffy `display: none`). Two things follow from that, and the bug is almost certainly one of them:

- **A `display: none` subtree is collapsed to zero size at the top-left by taffy**, so its bounds are stale/zero. `component::paint_child` skips hidden children for exactly this reason — *"painting it would stamp its (stale, overlapping) contents there"*. A container with a **bespoke paint loop** that iterates `base.children` directly, rather than through `paint_child`, will draw them. `Pane` and `DockFrame` are called out in that function's doc as the ones that must reuse it; check every paint loop on the path from the sidebar down to the rows, including any added since.
- **Damage.** `collect_damage` (`heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs`) skips hidden subtrees, so the rows' *old* pixels are never invalidated when they become hidden. If the collapse is not repainting the region the rows occupied, the pile is stale pixels rather than a live paint — which the screenshot cannot distinguish from the first cause.

# How to tell the two apart before fixing

Paint the collapsed tree into a `Scene` headlessly and read the `DrawCommand::Text` entries with their rects (the pattern `heca-grid-ui/tests/phase_a.rs` uses throughout). If the texts are **in** the scene, it is a paint loop; if they are absent, it is damage, and the fix is in the host's repaint rect.

# Verification

Antonio drives the showcase: collapse and expand both groups repeatedly, and scroll while collapsed. A headless test that asserts a collapsed group emits no text for its rows is the regression guard.

tasks.title: A row's hover lights its label but not its icon, and a toast's top margin lets the hover through to the widget behind
tasks.description:
Two hover defects Antonio reported driving the showcase (2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10). Filed together because both are about **which rect a hover belongs to**, and the second is the same question a `ToastStack` answers for its cards.

# 1. Hover highlights the label, not the icon

Hovering a row lights the text but leaves the leading `Icon` unlit. Expected: the whole row reads as hovered, icon included.

Hover is a **framework** fact now (F004/P084/T394): `pointer::update_hover` sets `PointerState::hovered` on the target's **whole ancestor chain**, CSS `:hover`-style, so a `Row` is hovered when the `Label` inside it is. So the row's hover state is almost certainly correct and the **paint** is not: the row publishes one content colour per frame via `PaintCx::with_content_color`, and an unstyled `Label`/`Icon` child pulls it. Check whether the `Icon` in that row was given an **explicit** colour at construction — an explicitly coloured child does not inherit, by design. `heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs` builds pane rows with `Icon::new(info.icon).size(14.0).color(theme.colors.foreground)`, which is exactly that shape.

If that is it, the fix is at the call site (drop the explicit colour so the icon inherits the row's state colour), not in the widget — but confirm before changing, because some icons are deliberately coloured (a git status marker must stay its own colour whatever the row does).

# 2. A toast's top margin highlights the widget underneath

Hovering near the **top edge** of a toast card lights the widget behind it instead of the card.

`ToastStack` (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast_stack.rs`) reports `hit_bounds()` as the **union of its cards' rects** and routes the pointer to the card under the cursor by hand in `on_event_capture` — the toasts are not `base.children`, they live in `entries`, reconciled by id. A point inside the union but outside every card returns `Handled::No` and falls through, which is what puts the hover on the page behind.

So the question is whether the point being hovered is inside the card's **drawn** area but outside its **bounds** — a card draws a glow and a shadow outside its rect, and `Toast`'s own margin/gap sit between cards. Measure it: paint the stack and compare the card's `DrawCommand` rects against `e.toast.base().bounds`.

**Related, and worth doing at the same time:** `ToastStack` keeping its cards outside `base.children` is the reason it hand-delivers events at all. Making them real children would delete that whole method and let the framework route to them — that is the treatment `ContextMenu` got in T395 and it is written into F004/P084/T400's notes as the remaining shape for the overlay widgets.

# Verification

Antonio drives it: hover along a row including its icon, and along a toast's top edge with a widget behind it.
